chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥamzah, from his father, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:

When Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) was brought to al-Shām, to Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and arrived at his door, he said to his companions and those of Banī Umayyah who were in his presence, "When you see that I have rebuked Muhammad ibn ʿAlī, then you see that I have fallen silent, let each man among you turn against him and rebuke him." Then he ordered that permission be granted for him.

So when Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) entered upon him, he said with his hand, "Peace be upon you," and thus included them all in the greeting. Then he sat down. Hishām became even more enraged at him because he had not greeted him with the caliphal salutation and had sat without permission. So he turned to rebuking him and among what he said to him was: "O Muhammad ibn ʿAlī, a man from among you continues to split the staff of the Muslims, call people to himself, and claim that he is the Imam, out of foolishness and little knowledge." And he rebuked him with whatever he wished to rebuke him with.

When he fell silent, the people turned against him, one man after another rebuking him, until the last of them had finished. Then when the people fell silent, he (عليه السلام) rose standing and said, "O people, where are you going, and where are you being led? Through us Allah guided your first ones, and through us He will conclude with your last ones. If there is for you a kingdom brought forward, then indeed for us there is a kingdom deferred; and there is no kingdom after our kingdom, because we are the people of the ultimate end." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“And the end is for the Godwary.”

So he ordered that he be taken to prison. When he came to the prison, he spoke, and there did not remain a man in the prison except that he became drawn to him and inclined toward him. Then the keeper of the prison came to Hishām and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I fear for you from the people of al-Shām, lest they come between you and this authority of yours." Then he informed him of his affair. So he ordered regarding him, and he and his companions were carried on the postal mounts to be returned to al-Madinah. And he ordered that the markets not be opened to them, and he cut them off from food and drink.

So they traveled for three days finding neither food nor drink, until they came to Madyan. Then the gate of the city was closed against them, and his companions complained of hunger and thirst. He said: So he climbed a mountain to overlook them and said in the loudest of his voice, "O people of the city whose inhabitants are unjust, I am the remnant of Allah." Allah says:
“The remnant of Allah is better for you, if you are believers, and I am not a keeper over you.”

He said: And there was among them an elderly shaykh. He came to them and said, "O my people, by Allah, this is the call of Shuʿayb the Prophet. By Allah, if you do not bring out to this man the market goods, you will surely be seized from above you and from beneath your feet. So believe me this once and obey me, and call me a liar in whatever you undertake afterward, for indeed I am a sincere adviser to you."

He said: So they hurried and brought out the market goods to Muhammad ibn ʿAlī and his companions. Then news of the shaykh reached Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, so he sent for him and had him taken away, and it was not known what he did with him.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (عليه السلام), the central figure of the report
key_terms.الْأَسْوَاقُ: Market provisions or goods withheld and later brought out
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The divinely designated leader claimed and defended in the report’s polemical exchange
key_terms.الْحَبْسِ: The prison to which the Imam was sent
key_terms.الْعَاقِبَةُ: The ultimate end or final outcome, identified as belonging to the Godwary
key_terms.الْمُتَّقِينَ: Those who possess taqwa; the Godwary who attain the good end
key_terms.بَقِيَّةُ اللَّهِ: The remnant of Allah, invoked by the Imam through Qur’anic wording
key_terms.هِشَامِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ: The Umayyad ruler before whom the Imam was brought

ai.seo_question: What happened when Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (عليه السلام) was brought before Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik?
ai.summary: This report narrates the confrontation of Imam Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAlī al-Baqir (عليه السلام) with Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, the Imam’s declaration of the divinely guided status of Ahl al-Bayt, and his citation of Qur’anic verses concerning the final outcome for the Godwary and the remnant of Allah. It also recounts his imprisonment, the effect of his words on others, and the events on the return journey when the people of a town were moved to provide aid.
